transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Li (Redwood CSM), Emma Rodriguez (Cedar Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Cedar Platform Eng), Nina Park (Cedar Head of Data), Oliver Grant (Cedar SRE), Samira Khan (Cedar Finance)

Summary: QBR and health check. Covered usage/cost trends, reliability incidents, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, data residency and audit requests, roadmap alignment for recommender v2.

Topics: usage and spend, latency incidents (2026-09 promo spike), KV cache + batching tuning, Dedicated capacity sizing, SOC2 / KMS, next steps and action items.

Action items (recap at end): Jordan to send deck; Priya to run benchmarks; Marcus to share test env; Emma to confirm targets.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone uh thanks for joining our qbr for cedar, uh i'm jordan from redwood inference, and with me is priya and alex. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Emma: pretty good, thanks. we have samira and oliver on the line too. big day for us, finalizing budget.
[00:12] Jordan: great, goal for today is to review last quarter's usage, costs, any reliability issues and align on q4 roadmap and action items. sound good?
[00:20] Marcus: yep that's the plan. we had a pretty rough promo last month, saw latency spikes and some 5xxs during the evening window.
[00:27] Priya: thanks for flagging that, marcus — do you have the spike times and sample logs? that helps us triage whether it was batching/queue or kernel fallback.
[00:35] Marcus: i do, i'll paste a snippet after, but it looks like the traffic pattern briefly doubled and we saw token rate ramp up; our prefix cache hit rate dropped.
[00:44] Nina: also noticed model version drift — sometimes requests hit the v1 alpha instead of v2 recommender, so a little inconsistency.
[00:51] Jordan: ok makes sense — some things to call out from our side in the deck: usage rose 42% q/q, cost per 1k tokens increased about 8% because of longer contexts during promo, and KV cache hit-rate fell from ~78% to 54% during the spike.
[01:10] Emma: that matches our internal numbers. finance is worried about the jump — samira is on the line to understand options.
[01:18] Samira: hi — yes the finance ask is can we cap monthly spend or move to dedicated reserved to flatten costs.
[01:24] Jordan: good question. we can model reserved capacity — usually dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit costs at commit — but you'll trade flexibility.
[01:33] Priya: technically, if you pin recommender v2 to a Dedicated pool and enable aggressive kv caching + pre-warm, you should see tail latency improve and effective cost per inference drop. the burst policy can handle promo traffic but there are limits.
[01:45] Marcus: are there any specific kernel or quantization changes we should make? we currently run a mixed-precision quantized variant.
[01:51] Priya: from what i saw in your telemetry, we recommend switching to the 8-bit QAT profile for v2 and enabling the alternate attention kernel for long sequences. that reduces memory pressure and keeps kv cache warm; i'll include exact params in the benchmark plan.
[02:07] Oliver: quick question on private deployment — we have a compliance push for data residency in EU next year, is your private plan ready?
[02:14] Alex: yes, we have a private offering (V P C and on-prem) with KMS integrations and audit logs; i'll share the architecture diagram and SOC2 artifacts in the follow-up.
[02:24] Emma: do you have customer references for on-prem?
[02:27] Alex: a few — i'll include anonymized references and a short case study.
[02:31] Jordan: moving on to reliability details — there were two incidents in sept, one during the promo which was the big one and an unrelated region failover that lasted about 12 minutes.
[02:40] Priya: the region failover was a routing misconfiguration during a provider maintenance; we have a new routing policy to avoid primary->secondary thrash, which we rolled out last week.
[02:50] Marcus: saw the routing change — latency was better on the new policy, thumbs up.
[02:53] Nina: the model rollout confusion — why did some traffic hit v1-alpha? can we pin traffic during rollout?
[02:58] Priya: yep, we support canary and A/B rollouts. looks like your deploy script used a tag that matched both variants; i'll work with marcus to tighten the selectors.
[03:08] Emma: about cost modeling — what's the best lever to recommend to our execs? we need predictability.
[03:14] Jordan: for predictability it's usually reserved capacity + model quantization + KV caching. we'll prepare a cost model with committed vs on-demand scenarios.
[03:22] Samira: and is there a way to get alerts when we approach a burn threshold?
[03:26] Alex: yes, we can add budget alerts and per-route token quotas; we'll propose thresholds in the deck.
[03:31] [04:00] Jordan: (slides) slide 5 shows usage trends by route — recommenders is 62% of tokens, chat support 22%, embeddings 16%.
[04:14] Emma: that aligns. recommender traffic is the heavy hitter during promos.
[04:20] Priya: on the performance side, i'd like to propose a benchmark run: we spin up a Dedicated pool sized for 3x normal promo qps, run live-ish traffic replay using your sample payloads, and measure tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency.
[04:34] Marcus: 3x sounds reasonable for planning. i'll provide the sample payloads and a replay window (about 2 hours).
[04:40] Priya: perfect. i'll include the exact configs: batch size, pre-warm, KV cache TTL and the quantization profile.
[04:48] Emma: what about data retention and logs — compliance wants 12 month logs and audit trail.
[04:54] Alex: we support configurable retention and can export audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules; we'll include an example retention policy.
[04:59] Oliver: any PII concerns for the logs? we need token redaction in transit.
[05:05] Priya: tokens are encrypted in transit; redaction is possible at the ingestion layer, but we typically recommend maintaining raw logs in a secured bucket with ACLs and masking in downstream systems.
[05:16] [06:00] Jordan: okay, let's walk through the roadmap alignment — cedar's recommender v2 deployment is planned for late q4, and you'd like Redwood to support the rollout and run benchmarks before GA.
[06:11] Emma: yes, and we want to avoid the same promo issues.
[06:15] Jordan: timeline proposal: benchmark week of 10/26, cost model delivered 10/22, architecture + SOC2 docs delivered 10/21, follow-up sync 11/02 to review benchmark results.
[06:29] Marcus: that timeline works for engineering.
[06:31] Samira: finance needs the committed pricing scenarios by 10/22 to close the budget.
[06:35] Jordan: understood, we'll prioritize the cost breakdown.
[06:38] [15:00] Priya: small note about batch sizing — during high concurrency you might want to cap max batching time to reduce p99 tail for short queries. i'll include that in configs.
[15:10] Marcus: yes our support queries are short, batching needs to be tuned per-route.
[15:15] Nina: is there a recommended pre-warm strategy? we saw cold starts affect p95 in the morning.
[15:21] Priya: pre-warm via a small constant background traffic and keep a warm pool for the recommender; also use cache persistence between instances when possible.
[15:30] Emma: what's the expected unit cost improvement if we move to Dedicated with quantization?
[15:36] Jordan: rough ballpark — for your workload we estimate 20-30% lower cost per effective inference at commit levels you're targeting, but we'll give precise numbers in the cost model.
[15:48] Samira: we'll review that with procurement.
[15:52] [30:00] Jordan: okay, any blockers from cedar side for the benchmark?
[30:05] Marcus: need to set up test keys and an ephemeral S3 for logs; we'll do that early next week.
[30:11] Marcus: also need to confirm RPS patterns for promos — we'll share the traffic window.
[30:16] Priya: great, i'll prepare a benchmark plan doc with expected metrics: throughput, p50/p95/p99, memory usage, cache hit-rate, and cost per 1k tokens.
[30:26] Nina: one more ask — can we get a sample alert runbook for post-deploy incidents? our on-call needs a playbook.
[30:33] Alex: yes, we'll send a runbook template and adapt it to your alerting stack (pagerduty/slack).
[30:38] Emma: perfect.
[30:41] [40:00] Jordan: final recap: action items are in the deck and will be emailed. timeline: cost model 10/22, infra docs and SOC2 10/21, benchmark week 10/26, follow-up 11/02.
[40:15] Emma: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[40:19] Samira: thanks, please cc procurement.
[40:22] Jordan: will do, i'll send the deck and attach the SOC2 link and architecture diagram.
[40:28] Marcus: thanks, talk soon.
[40:30] [47:30] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (V P C, kv cash) and some speaker overlap. Links referenced: QBR deck (link to be sent), SOC2 pack (link to be sent), benchmark plan (link to be created).
